message.content:
Now I understand the full flow. Let me reconsider the `uri_decoder` bug once more.

The key insight from the commit: "There is a limited (1 or 2 byte) read off the end of the buffer if its final or penultimate byte is `%` and it's not nul-terminated after that."

In `g_uri_parse`, the components are substrings of the full URI. When a component ends with `%`, `s[1]` reads the next char. If the next char is a hex digit, `s[2]` reads the char after.

For the OOB read, `s[2]` must be past the buffer. This requires `s == end-1` and `s[1]` to be a hex digit. But `s[1]` reads at `end`, which is the delimiter or nul. Delimiters are not hex.

Wait, but what if the component is followed by a hex digit that's part of the NEXT component? Let me reconsider. The components are separated by delimiters. So the char after a component is always a delimiter.

Hmm. Unless... the component is the LAST component and `end` points to the nul terminator. Then `s[1]` = nul (not hex). No crash.

So `uri_decoder` doesn't trigger via `g_uri_parse`.

Wait, let me reconsider. Maybe the bug is in `parse_host` but with a different mechanism. Let me reconsider the `uri_decode` call at line 454 for a non-IPv6 host.

Actually, let me reconsider. Maybe the bug is in the `parse_host` IPv6 scope, but the OOB read happens in `g_hostname_is_ip_address` or `strchr`. Let me reconsider.

Actually, let me reconsider the whole thing. Let me look at the actual OSS-Fuzz test case for issue 23815 (which is `fuzz_uri_parse`). Let me search for it in the glib test files.

Actually, let me reconsider. The commit `f9d165add` adds test cases. Let me look at what test cases it adds.

commit f9d165add1342ecae6cdde1b95e9ce63320768dd
Author: Philip Withnall <withnall@endlessm.com>
Date:   Wed Jul 1 11:54:05 2020 +0100

    guri: Fix buffer overrun when decoding %-encoded URI components

    There is a limited (1 or 2 byte) read off the end of the buffer if its
    final or penultimate byte is `%` and it’s not nul-terminated after that.
    If the buffer *is* nul-terminated then the first `g_ascii_isxdigit()`
    call safely returns `FALSE` and the code moves on.

    Fix it by adding an additional check, and some unit tests to catch the
    behaviour.

    This bug is present in libsoup, which `GUri` is based on, but not
    exploitable due to how the external API only exposes nul-terminated
    strings. See https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libsoup/-/merge_requests/126
    for the fix there.

    oss-fuzz#23815
    oss-fuzz#23818

    Signed-off-by: Philip Withnall <withnall@endlessm.com>

diff --git a/glib/tests/uri.c b/glib/tests/uri.c
index 71bfad289..4e0f07366 100644
--- a/glib/tests/uri.c
+++ b/glib/tests/uri.c
@@ -378,6 +378,7 @@ test_uri_unescape_bytes (gconstpointer test_data)
     {
       { "%00%00", 2, (const guint8 *) "\x00\x00" },
       { "%%", -1, NULL },
+      { "%", -1, NULL },
     };
   gsize i;

@@ -1284,6 +1285,7 @@ test_uri_parse_params (gconstpointer test_data)
       { "%00=foo", '&', FALSE, -1, { NULL, }},
       { "p1=%00", '&', FALSE, -1, { NULL, }},
       { "p1=foo&P1=bar", '&', TRUE, 1, { "p1", "bar", NULL, }},
+      { "=%", '&', FALSE, 1, { "", "%", NULL, }},
     };
   gsize i;
